title: Lightweight AI Scheduling for Ultra-Fast Decision Making in Autonomous IoT Devices
authors: Gudivada Dinesh; Kola Tarun; N. Sugitha
venue: International Conference on Emerging Research in Computational Science (ICERCS)
abstract: Autonomous Internet-of-Things (IoT) devices deployed at the extreme edge—such as nano-drones, industrial actuators, and nanosatellites—must make safety-critical decisions within sub-millisecond deadlines while operating under stringent energy, memory, and thermal constraints [9]. Classical real-time scheduling policies such as Earliest Deadline First (EDF) or Rate Monotonic (RM) are computationally lightweight but brittle under non-stationary workloads, bursty sensor streams, and varying wireless channel dynamics [1], [2]. Conversely, modern Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) approaches offer adaptivity but typically require computational resources (GPUs, large memory) unavailable on microcontroller-class hardware [3], [7], [8]. This paper bridges this gap by proposing a Hybrid Lightweight AI Scheduler (H-LAIS). H-LAIS combines a deterministic rule-based safety envelope, a highly quantized tiny neural inference core (distilled from a heavy teacher policy), and an ultra-compact RL adaptation layer to achieve ultra-fast, adaptive decision-making. The scheduler operates entirely on-device, consuming less than 15 kB of RAM and 30 kB of flash memory [4], [10]. The scheduling problem is formulated as a Constrained Markov Decision Process (CMDP) and solved using a Lagrangian relaxation technique that jointly accounts for deadline satisfaction, energy consumption, and context-aware urgency [13], [17]. Cycle-accurate simulations and hardware-in-the-loop experiments on an ARM Cortex-M4 platform demonstrate that H-LAIS reduces deadline misses by up to 41.3% and energy per decision by 32.7% compared to classical heuristics, while maintaining a worst-case inference latency under 40 µs. Furthermore, a Lyapunov stability analysis is provided to argue queue boundedness [17], and an extensive ablation study validates the system’s robustness.

title: Meta-Policy-Based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Dynamic UAV Networks: Resolving Hybrid Action Spaces and Non-Stationarity
authors: Zifeng Dai; Hui Xie; Shengjun Wei; Changzhen Hu
abstract: Synergistically optimizing cooperative trajectory and task offloading in UAV-assisted Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) is a critical challenge for 6G-enabled ubiquitous computing. However, existing multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) frameworks suffer from severe gradient scale mismatch in hybrid action spaces, multiplier oscillations under non-convex fairness constraints, and strategic non-stationarity in dynamic environments. This paper proposes MAPA-MARL, a novel meta-policy framework designed to structurally resolve these bottlenecks. Specifically, we formulate the joint optimization as a Constrained Markov Decision Process (CMDP) and introduce a PID-Lagrangian mechanism to enforce Jain's Fairness Index, utilizing Exponential Moving Average (EMA) filtered derivative damping to safely suppress the instability typical of traditional dual ascent. To handle the hybrid decision-making space, we develop a Dual-Head Actor architecture integrated with a Variance-Bounded Zero-temperature Gumbel-Rao (ZGR) estimator. This provides a low-variance empirical gradient proxy, effectively mitigating the gradient variance explosion and preventing the meta-initialization collapse induced by conventional discrete relaxations. Furthermore, a Sparsity-Induced Inverse-Distance Soft-Mask is proposed; rather than merely reducing computational complexity, it acts as a topological regularizer to block polluted gradients from distant agents, thereby stabilizing local coordination. To anchor convergence against peer-evolution without inter-UAV parameter sharing, we integrate an RNN-based implicit opponent modeling module augmented with Hessian-Vector Product (HVP) second-order curvature compensation. Extensive simulations demonstrate that MAPA-MARL achieves superior Pareto efficiency with a minimal 18.5 MB memory footprint and millisecond-level onboard inference latency, confirming its robust viability for resource-constrained edge deployment.

title: A WebRTC-Based Architecture for Remote Monitoring of Mobile Robots
authors: Gabriel Víctor M. Muniz; Michel Melo da Silva; Alexandre Santos Brandao
abstract: Remote monitoring and teleoperation of robotic systems over the Internet require low-latency and bandwidth-efficient video transmission to ensure safe and responsive control. This article presents the development and experimental validation of a real-time video streaming architecture based on the WebRTC protocol, integrated into the ROS ecosystem using GStreamer. The proposed solution exploits hardware-accelerated video encoding on an NVIDIA Jetson Nano to optimize the transmission of RGB-D camera data over public networks. Connectivity across distinct networks and restrictive NAT and firewall environments is ensured through a TURN-assisted signaling mechanism. Experimental results evaluate glass-to-glass latency and bandwidth consumption, comparing the performance of H.264 and VP8 codecs at multiple video resolutions. The results demonstrate that hardware-accelerated H.264 significantly reduces bandwidth usage while maintaining low and stable latency suitable for real-time robotic teleoperation, whereas VP8 is only viable at low resolutions. Overall, the proposed architecture provides a feasible solution for remote robotic monitoring and control over public networks.

title: Lucio at RoboCup@Home: An Open-Hardware Mobile Manipulator with Modular Software and On-Device LLM Planning
authors: Dongwoon Song; Taewoong Kang; Shady Nasrat; Joonyoung Kim; Minseong Jo; Gijae Ahn; Seonil Lee; Seung‐Joon Yi
venue: IEEE-RAS International Conference on Humanoid Robots (Humanoids)
abstract: We present Lucio, a competition-validated, open-hardware mobile manipulator designed to execute complex domestic tasks with robust autonomy and full on-device reasoning. Lucio combines a holonomic omnidirectional base, a 7-DoF Kinova Gen3 arm, and a Robotiq gripper with a modular ROS-based software framework that scales across wheeled, legged, and humanoid platforms. Its perception pipeline leverages YOLOv11, point-cloud filtering, and colored heightmap grasp sampling to perform reliable object detection and manipulation, even in cluttered environments. At the core of Lucio's high-level control is the Robotic Decision-Making Model (RDMM)―a 4-bit quantized large language model fine-tuned on 27,000 task plans and 1,300 multimodal instruction-action pairs derived from RoboCup@Home scenarios. Running entirely on an embedded Jetson Orin, RDMM enables low-latency natural language task execution without cloud reliance. Lucio was validated in two full RoboCup@Home seasons, consistently completing complex tasks such as Storing Groceries, Clean the Table, and General Purpose Service Robot with zero manual resets. We release Lucio's full hardware design, software stack, and simulation environments to support reproducible research in service robotics, task planning, and on-device LLM integration.

title: rMuscle: Robotic Muscle Memory for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Model Inference
authors: Kaijun Zhou; Zhiyang Li; Le Chen; Jinyu Gu
abstract: Factory work is a promising early scenario for embodied AI: assigning repetitive manual jobs to robots has clear economic payoff, and a structured station keeps the jobs tractable for current policies. Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models now dominate as the policy paradigm for these robots. The inference latency of VLA models directly affects robot responsiveness and motion smoothness. However, existing VLA inference frameworks do not fully exploit the characteristics of embodied workloads or account for the distinct bottlenecks across different stages of VLA inference. In this paper, we first characterize embodied workloads and identify substantial task similarity across repeated robot executions. We further find that such similarity extends beyond observations and action trajectories to internal model states. Drawing on these observations, we present rMuscle, a real-time VLA inference framework inspired by human muscle memory. It exploits cross-execution similarity through a dual-phase muscle-memory cache. The Context Cache reuses visual-token outputs to reduce computation, while the Action Cache reuses neuron activation patterns to reduce weight accesses. We keep both the cache memory footprint and access overhead low through online cache recomputation, sliding-window cache retrieval, and mask sharing across consecutive denoising steps. rMuscle achieves 1.29-1.42X speedup on RTX 4090 and Jetson Thor across LIBERO, RoboTwin, and physical manipulation tasks, while maintaining the original success rates on real-world robots.

title: MMEdge: Accelerating On-device Multimodal Inference via Pipelined Sensing and Encoding
authors: Runxi Huang; Mingxuan Yu; Mingyu Tsoi; Xiaomin Ouyang
abstract: Real-time multimodal inference on resource-constrained edge devices is essential for applications such as autonomous driving, human-computer interaction, and mobile health. However, prior work often overlooks the tight coupling between sensing dynamics and model execution, as well as the complex inter-modality dependencies. In this paper, we propose MMEdge, a new on-device multimodal inference framework based on pipelined sensing and encoding. Instead of waiting for complete sensor inputs, MMEdge decomposes the entire inference process into a sequence of fine-grained sensing and encoding units, allowing computation to proceed incrementally as data arrive. MMEdge also introduces a lightweight but effective temporal aggregation module that captures rich temporal dynamics across different pipelined units to maintain accuracy performance. Such pipelined design also opens up opportunities for fine-grained cross-modal optimization and early decision-making during inference. To further enhance system performance under resource variability and input data complexity, MMEdge incorporates an adaptive multimodal configuration optimizer that dynamically selects optimal sensing and model configurations for each modality under latency constraints, and a cross-modal speculative skipping mechanism that bypasses future units of slower modalities when early predictions reach sufficient confidence. We evaluate MMEdge using two public multimodal datasets and deploy it on a real-world unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based multimodal testbed. The results show that MMEdge significantly reduces end-to-end latency while maintaining high task accuracy across various system and data dynamics. A video demonstration of MMEdge’s performance in real world is available at https://youtu.be/qRew7sT-iWw.

title: Open-Source AI Stack for CubeSat Autonomous Navigation
authors: Gerald Enrique Nelson Mc Kenzie
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Open-Source AI Stack for CubeSat Autonomous Navigation presents a complete framework for deploying deep reinforcement learning on resource-constrained spacecraft. The paper details a Hierarchical TD3 architecture trained on consumer GPUs (NVIDIA 4070 Super) and optimized for flight hardware with only 256MB RAM. It covers the full pipeline—from TensorFlow/PyTorch training through quantization and TensorFlow Lite deployment on Xilinx Zynq-7020 and Jetson Nano platforms. Key contributions include multi-sensor fusion via Python I2C/UART interfaces, computer vision-based optical navigation, and a four-tier safety architecture ensuring fault tolerance during communication blackouts. Validated through hardware-in-the-loop testing, this open-source stack enables sub-meter precision satellite rendezvous while maintaining real-time inference within severe power and memory constraints typical of nanosatellite missions.

title: Hybrid Adaptive MPC with Edge AI for 6-DoF Industrial Robotic Manipulators
authors: Claudio Urrea
abstract: Autonomous robotic manipulators in industrial environments face significant challenges, including time-varying payloads, multi-source disturbances, and real-time computational constraints. Traditional model predictive control frameworks degrade by over 40% under model uncertainties, while conventional adaptive techniques exhibit convergence times incompatible with industrial cycles. This work presents a hybrid adaptive model predictive control framework integrating edge artificial intelligence with dual-stage parameter estimation for 6-DoF industrial manipulators. The approach combines recursive least squares with a resource-optimized neural network (three layers, 32 neurons, 1.2). This performance surpasses recent adaptive control methods while maintaining proven stability guarantees. Hardware validation under realistic industrial conditions remains necessary to confirm practical applicability.

title: Graph convolutional reinforcement learning for multi-agent coordination in smart home environments: an intelligent framework for elderly care assistance
authors: Thanh Sơn Lê; Huu Sy Le; Nguyen Tan Viet Tuyen; Nguyen Tan Viet Tuyen
abstract: The rapid aging of global populations presents unprecedented challenges for elderly care systems, particularly for individuals living independently who require assistance with daily activities. This paper presents a novel Graph Convolutional Reinforcement Learning (GCRL) framework for multi-agent coordination in smart home environments. Our approach addresses five fundamental gaps in existing systems: unified relational representations for heterogeneous agents and objects, efficient learned coordination without centralized bottlenecks, embodied execution of physical assistance tasks, explicit agent-object heterogeneity modeling, and computational efficiency. The framework models the environments as dynamic heterogeneous graphs where agents and interactive objects are represented as nodes with spatial proximity defining edges, enabling relational reasoning through graph convolutional networks with attention mechanisms for implicit coordination. We employ Proximal Policy Optimization combined with experience replay to achieve stable multi-agent training, allowing agents to learn cooperative behaviors through environmental interaction without predefined communication protocols. Experiments in the AI2-THOR simulator across four elderly care scenarios demonstrate that, within this simulation-based evaluation, GCRL achieves an 80.03±1.8% overall success rate (mean ± standard deviation across three seeds) with 28.35 average steps to completion, substantially outperforming baseline methods including SMART-LLM (57.43±3.0%), SYNERGY (64.33±2.4%), and LaMMA-P (65.98±2.6%), while maintaining real-time inference capabilities and memory requirements suitable for privacy-preserving edge deployment in residential environments. Real-world validation on a physical assistive platform is identified as the immediate next research step.

title: Event-based Agile Object Catching with a Quadrupedal Robot
authors: Benedek Forrai; Takahiro Miki; Daniel Gehrig; Marco Hutter; Davide Scaramuzza
venue: Proceedings - IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation/Proceedings
abstract: Quadrupedal robots are conquering various applications in indoor and outdoor environments due to their capability to navigate challenging uneven terrains. Exteroceptive information greatly enhances this capability since perceiving their surroundings allows them to adapt their controller and thus achieve higher levels of robustness. However, sensors such as LiDARs and RGB cameras do not provide sufficient information to quickly and precisely react in a highly dynamic environment since they suffer from a bandwidth-latency trade-off. They require significant bandwidth at high frame rates while featuring significant perceptual latency at lower frame rates, thereby limiting their versatility on resource constrained platforms. In this work, we tackle this problem by equipping our quadruped with an event camera, which does not suffer from this tradeoff due to its asynchronous and sparse operation. In leveraging the low latency of the events, we push the limits of quadruped agility and demonstrate high-speed ball catching for the first time. We show that our quadruped equipped with an event-camera can catch objects with speeds up to 15 m/s from 4 meters, with a success rate of 83%. Using a VGA event camera, our method runs at 100 Hz on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin.

title: Explainable Attention-GRU for Real-Time Multi-Modal IoT Safety Monitoring
authors: Kommu Kishore Babu; Dr.R.Venkatesan; K. Ramalakshmi
venue: International Conference on Electronics and Sustainable Communication Systems (ICESC)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) has been rapidly expanding and bringing transformative features to the monitoring of vulnerable populations, notably in the area of women safety and elderly care. Yet, the computational and memory burden of state-of-the-art deep learning architectures is a major challenge for operating these predictive models on the edge devices with limited resources. Moreover, conventional deep neural networks are "black-box" models, and in safety-critical applications, such as medical settings, where the mechanism behind an emergency alert is as crucial as the alert itself, trust and clinical compliance are important issues that should not be overlooked. In this paper, a novel hybrid architecture is proposed to combine an Attention-Augmented Gated Recurrent Unit (A-GRU) with a Neuro-Symbolic Explainability Framework (NSEF). The system proposed not only has the strict computation efficiency for edge deployment in low power environments, but it can also produce human readable, rule-based explanations for automated safety interventions. The proposed A-GRU-NSEF framework has been evaluated on a synthetic hybrid dataset combining kinematic patterns obtained from the MobiAct v2 and physiological stress patterns obtained from WESAD, and it yields an excellent accuracy of 98.54%, while having a very low edge inference latency of 42.3 ms on an NVIDIA Jetson Nano platform when compiled using TensorRT. The results demonstrate a scalable, computationally efficient, and completely transparent paradigm for proactive edge-based threat assessment.

title: Multimodal AI Architectures for Real-Time Decision-Making in Autonomous Systems
authors: Yaser Issam Hamodi; Abdul Monem S. Rahma; Darin Shafek; Adham Mohsen Saeed; Тetiana Sоmkіnа
venue: Communications in computer and information science

title: Graph convolutional reinforcement learning for multi-agent coordination in smart home environments: an intelligent framework for elderly care assistance
authors: Thanh Son Le; Huu Sy Le; Tan Duy Le; Nguyen Thi Kim Tuyen
abstract: The rapid aging of global populations presents unprecedented challenges for elderly care systems, particularly for individuals living independently who require assistance with daily activities. This paper presents a novel Graph Convolutional Reinforcement Learning (GCRL) framework for multi-agent coordination in smart home environments. Our approach addresses five fundamental gaps in existing systems: unified relational representations for heterogeneous agents and objects, efficient learned coordination without centralized bottlenecks, embodied execution of physical assistance tasks, explicit agent-object heterogeneity modeling, and computational efficiency. The framework models the environments as dynamic heterogeneous graphs where agents and interactive objects are represented as nodes with spatial proximity defining edges, enabling relational reasoning through graph convolutional networks with attention mechanisms for implicit coordination. We employ Proximal Policy Optimization combined with experience replay to achieve stable multi-agent training, allowing agents to learn cooperative behaviors through environmental interaction without predefined communication protocols. Experiments in the AI2-THOR simulator across four elderly care scenarios demonstrate that, within this simulation-based evaluation, GCRL achieves an 80.03±1.8% overall success rate (mean ± standard deviation across three seeds) with 28.35 average steps to completion, substantially outperforming baseline methods including SMART-LLM (57.43±3.0%), SYNERGY (64.33±2.4%), and LaMMA-P (65.98±2.6%), while maintaining real-time inference capabilities and memory requirements suitable for privacy-preserving edge deployment in residential environments. Real-world validation on a physical assistive platform is identified as the immediate next research step.

title: Vision Language Models on the Edge for Real-Time Robotic Perception
authors: Sarat Ahmad; Maryam Hafeez; Syed Ali Raza Zaidi
abstract: Vision–Language Models (VLMs) enable multimodal reasoning for robotic perception and interaction, but their deployment in real-world systems remains constrained by latency, limited onboard resources, and privacy risks of cloud offloading. Edge intelligence within 6G, particularly Open RAN and Multi-access Edge Computing (MEC), offers a pathway to address these challenges by bringing computation closer to the data source. This work investigates the deployment of VLMs on ORAN/MEC infrastructure using the Unitree G1 humanoid robot as an embodied testbed. We design a WebRTC-based pipeline that streams multimodal data to an edge node and evaluate LLaMA-3.2-11B-Vision-Instruct deployed at the edge versus in the cloud under real-time conditions. Our results show that edge deployment preserves near-cloud accuracy while reducing end-to-end latency by 5%. We further evaluate Qwen2-VL-2BInstruct, a compact model optimized for resource-constrained environments, which achieves sub-second responsiveness, cutting latency by more than half but at the cost of accuracy.

title: AUTONOMOUS AI AGENTS FOR REAL-TIME PROCESS DISCOVERY AND OPTIMIZATION
authors: S.Gowsalya S.Gowsalya; Dr.V.Ramya Dr.V.Ramya; Dr. R. Kabilan
venue: JOURNAL OF ADVANCE AND FUTURE RESEARCH
abstract: With the introduction of autonomous AI agents, process mining has been transformed, enabling the discovery, monitoring, and optimization of complex workflows in business and industry in real time. Traditional PM methods require fixed event logs, manual data entry and intervention, and are not suitable for dynamic, high-velocity environments such as supply chains, manufacturing, and digital services. In this paper, we introduce Agentic Real-Time Process Optimizer (ARPO). This multi-agent framework automates process handling using large language models (LLMs), graph neural networks (GNNs), and reinforcement learning (RL). ARPO uses hierarchical agents to perceive streaming data, discover process models, detect anomalies, and optimize the pathways in real-time, improving efficiency by up to 35% in simulated industrial scenarios. Benchmarks such as BPI Challenge datasets and custom IoT streams have proven to be highly adaptable (F1-score: 0.92) and have low latency (< 50 ms per event). The main contributions of this work are: scalability of agent architecture for edge deployment, integration of explainable AI (XAI) for transparent decisions, and empirical validation of the work in manufacturing use cases. It is a book that brings together both agentic AI and process mining to create resilient and self-optimizing systems in the face of the challenges of Industry 5.0.

title: Concurrent Video-Stream Workload and Sustained Thermal Conditions Affect the Latency and Real-Time Performance of Object Detection on the NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano
authors: Sumedh Chekka
abstract: Autonomous vehicles depend on perception systems that must detect objects accurately and quickly enough to support real-time decision-making. Edge platforms such as the NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano allow this perception to run directly on a vehicle, but their ability to sustain real-time performance under increasing computational and thermal demands remains uncertain. This study examines how the number of concurrent video streams and sustained thermal load affect the inference latency and pipeline latency of a You Only Look Once (YOLO) object detector running locally on a Jetson Orin Nano. The same prerecorded dashcam video was processed using one, two, and three simultaneous feeds, and hardware measurements, including graphics processing unit (GPU) utilization and temperature, were recorded under low and high temperature conditions. Condition-level values were calculated as the mean ± standard deviation across three 60-s trials for each workload condition. Mean pipeline latency rose from 83.91 ± 5.79 ms with one feed to 101.13 ± 2.95 ms with two feeds and 129.67 ± 3.48 ms with three feeds, crossing a commonly used 100 ms real-time reference (no vehicle response was measured). Across the three trials for each workload condition, 1.50 ± 0.12% of frames exceeded 100 ms with one feed, 43.75 ± 4.56% with two feeds, and 81.30 ± 2.90% with three feeds; mean 99th percentile (p99) pipeline latency was 105.15 ± 8.42 ms, 137.88 ± 1.75 ms, and 195.29 ± 9.13 ms, respectively. Inference latency increased less sharply than pipeline latency. Sustained thermal load raised GPU temperature but did not produce a comparably large increase in single-stream latency. These findings suggest that concurrent computational workload, more than sustained heat, constrains real-time object-detection performance on this platform.

title: CSI-Assisted Edge SLAM Testbed Platform for 5G Connected Unmanned Autonomous Vehicles
authors: Boris Radovanović; Saša Taloši; Srdjan Sobot; Dejan Vukobratović
venue: International Balkan Conference on Communications and Networking (BalkanCom)
abstract: The evolution from 5G towards 6G reinforces interest in connected robotics, where mobile robots offload compute-intensive tasks to edge servers over ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC) links. Simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM), a fundamental yet demanding robotics function, is increasingly considered for edge deployment within mobile edge computing (MEC) frameworks. In parallel, integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) enables the use of radio channel information, such as channel state information (CSI), as an additional sensing modality in radio-based SLAM. In this paper, we design and implement a CSI-assisted Edge SLAM testbed integrating a custom unmanned ground vehicle (UGV), a ROS2-based SLAM framework, and a 5G Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) system. The proposed architecture provides an end-to-end, cross-layer view of ROS2 sensor data streaming over 5G, explicitly enabling CSI exposure and integration into the SLAM pipeline. We analyze ROS2–DDS communication, RTPS packetization, and 5G user-plane transport, and discuss mechanisms for CSI extraction and delivery via O-RAN components. The platform enables realistic experimentation with communication-aware SLAM and reveals key challenges related to latency, data streaming, synchronization, and cross-system integration, providing insights for future 6G-enabled robotic platforms.

title: SecHOT-GNC: Security-Oriented Hardware- and OT-Aware Graph Neural Clustering for Attack-Chain Community Detection in Industrial Fiber Manufacturing Systems
authors: Liang Zhang; Fu Wang
abstract: Industrial fiber manufacturing systems increasingly rely on tightly coupled operational technology (OT) networks and heterogeneous hardware controllers, making them vulnerable to multi-stage attack chains that traverse cyber–physical dependencies. Existing graph-based security analytics often ignore hardware constraints and OT process semantics, leading to unstable communities, weak attack-chain consistency, and limited deployability on shop-floor compute. This paper proposes SecHOT-GNC, a security-oriented, hardware- and OT-aware graph neural clustering framework for attack-chain community detection in industrial fiber manufacturing. We model the plant as a multi-layer heterogeneous graph that integrates OT assets (PLCs, HMIs, drives, sensors), communication flows, process topology, and hardware attributes (resource budgets, firmware/OS class, interface types, timing constraints). SecHOT-GNC couples OT-aware message passing with a security-driven clustering objective that aligns communities with plausible attacker paths by jointly optimizing (i) attack-chain consistency, (ii) OT-process coherence, (iii) hardware feasibility under on-device constraints, and (iv) robustness to noisy/partial telemetry. The framework further produces interpretable community rationales via edge/feature attributions and yields community-level risk scores to support prioritization of defense actions. Experiments on industrial fiber manufacturing datasets and attack simulations demonstrate that SecHOT-GNC improves attack-chain community quality and stability over representative baselines, while maintaining practical inference latency and memory footprints suitable for edge/plant deployment.

title: Network-Independent Voice-Based Control for Autonomous Ground Vehicles in GNSS-Denied Environments
authors: Dr. Prasad Matam, Y Madhu Maheswara Reddy, Faizan Ahmed Siddiqui, Mir Kamran Ali
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: The operational reliability of autonomous ground vehicles in contested environments is fundamentally constrained by dependence on external communication infrastructure. In scenarios ranging from underground mining to extraterrestrial exploration, the absence of Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) signals and reliable network connectivity renders conventional teleoperation and cloud-dependent control architectures ineffective. This paper presents the design, implementation, and comprehensive field validation of a novel autonomous robotic vehicle that achieves robust voice-based navigation and control without any external network dependency. The system is architected to provide intuitive human-robot interaction in GNSS-denied, infrastructure-poor environments. The proposed system employs a hierarchical architecture comprising three core components: (1) an on-device speech recognition engine utilizing a custom-trained convolutional neural network with attention mechanism optimized for edge deployment on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin; (2) a transformer-based natural language understanding module that maps conversational commands to executable navigation primitives; and (3) a multi-modal perception stack integrating 3D LiDAR, stereo vision, and inertial sensing for simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) in unmapped environments. A formal command verification framework ensures that all voice directives are validated against real-time safety constraints before execution. Experimental evaluation was conducted across four distinct environmental conditions: a controlled laboratory setting, an urban canyon with multipath acoustic interference, a forested trail with ambient wind noise, and an abandoned underground mine shaft representing a GNSS-denied, high-noise operational scenario. The system achieved a mean command recognition accuracy of 94.7% across all environments, with a word error rate of 6.2% in the most challenging mine environment. End-to-end latency averaged 287 ms, enabling real-time responsive control. In autonomous navigation trials spanning 2.3 km of cumulative distance with zero network connectivity, the vehicle successfully executed 98.4% of issued navigation commands, with safety arbitration preventing 100% of potentially hazardous directives. The SLAM pipeline maintained localization accuracy within 0.12 m RMSE over extended trajectories.

title: Real-Time Object Detection for Autonomous Solar Farm Inspection via UAVs
authors: Javier Rodríguez-Vázquez; Inés Prieto-Centeno; Miguel Fernández-Cortizas; David Pérez-Saura; Martín Molina; Pascual Campoy
abstract: Robotic missions for solar farm inspection demand agile and precise object detection strategies. This paper introduces an innovative keypoint-based object detection framework specifically designed for real-time solar farm inspections with UAVs. Moving away from conventional bounding box or segmentation methods, our technique focuses on detecting the vertices of solar panels, which provides a richer granularity than traditional approaches. Drawing inspiration from CenterNet, our architecture is optimized for embedded platforms like the NVIDIA AGX Jetson Orin, achieving close to 60 FPS at a resolution of 1024 ×1376 pixels, thus outperforming the camera's operational frequency. Such a real-time capability is essential for efficient robotic operations in time-critical industrial asset inspection environments. The design of our model emphasizes reduced computational demand, positioning it as a practical solution for real-world deployment. Additionally, the integration of active learning strategies promises a considerable reduction in annotation efforts and strengthens the model's operational feasibility. In summary, our research emphasizes the advantages of keypoint-based object detection, offering a practical and effective approach for real-time solar farm inspections with UAVs.

title: Edge AI-Based Object Detection via Voice Recognition with an LLM-Based Emotional Assistant for Elderly Care Robots
authors: Sarra Ben Halima; Faten Ben Abdallah; -Joseph -Y. HAGGEGE
venue: International Journal of Information Technology and Computer Science
abstract: This paper presents a fully integrated, real-time assistive system that combines voice-based object recognition with a generative conversational interface, specifically designed to enhance elderly care through edge AI deployment. The proposed framework enables intuitive human–robot interaction in domestic environments by fusing natural language understanding, optimized visual detection, and local generative response. Voice commands are processed through a speech-to-text pipeline using the Google Web Speech API, with keyword extraction triggering object detection via a quantized YOLOv8n model accelerated through TensorRT with FP16 inference on an NVIDIA Jetson Nano. In parallel, a locally deployed generative AI assistant, executed entirely on-device, provides empathetic dialogue to support social engagement and emotional well-being. The proposed system adopts a hybrid edge architecture in which object detection, robot control, and LLM-based dialogue generation are executed on-device, while speech-to-text transcription relies on a cloud-based service. This generative interface is implemented as an LLM-based Emotional Assistant. The system achieves 13 FPS with an inference latency of 70 ms for object detection, 94.3% speech recognition accuracy, and an F1-score of 0.69 at a 0.5 confidence threshold. All AI components are executed on-board, preserving privacy for on- device processing while maintaining real-time responsiveness. Experimental validation confirms the effectiveness of deploying multimodal AI, including generative models, on resource-constrained hardware. This work lays the foundation for autonomous, voice-guided care robots that not only assist in locating objects but also engage users socially, promoting greater autonomy and quality of life for older adults.

title: Edge AI Integration for Adaptive Control in Embedded Robotics Platforms
authors: S. Bhaskar; Lakshmi Sree Lakshmanan
venue: International Conference of Advances in Engineering and Computing Technologies for Sustainable Development (AECTSD)
abstract: Robot-assisted surgery (RAS) has transformed joint and bone surgery. A major challenge in RAS is the segmentation of images to aid the surgery process, which requires huge computing and real-time analysis. The traditional applications of cloud systems might not be viable when it comes to long operations because of their increased latency and security concerns, as well as the need to have a good internet connection. Edge Artificial Intelligence (Edge AI) is a game-changing concept of robotics. Edge AI is especially suitable in situations when high processing and power consumption cannot be considered a feasible option, and low-latency response time is a must. This paper investigates edge AI image segmentation in RAS in orthopedic surgery. This paper examines how Edge AI enables the reduced reliance on external systems and minimization of the segmentation to the surgical location, and is reasonably accurate in real-time segmentation. This paper will discuss three deep learning (DL) technologies, namely, Transformer, DeepLabVe, and U-Net, that fulfill the edge design based on approaches such as quantization, trimming, and data distillation. Operative images would be best analyzed with a real-time analysis workflow that is founded on edge AI systems, including the NVIDIA Jetson Xavier and the Google Coral TPU. The findings of the study show that real-time predictions with Edge AI segmentation have a latency within 100 milliseconds and are highly accurate. The research issues explored include the generality of the systems used in working with different anatomies of patients, limitations on the hardware used, and legal adherence. Therefore, by enabling the fast, precise, and regional analysis of the image, Edge AI would enhance the quality of RAS in orthopedics. This would enhance patient outcomes and the accuracy of operations.

title: On-Device Preference Graph Reasoner for Personalized and Verifiable Home Automation
authors: S. Praveen Kumar
venue: National Journal of Ubiquitous Computing and Intelligent Environments
abstract: There is a need for intelligent decision-making to ensure personal privacy in the home and meet evolving preferences in a personalized home automation environment. Current cloud-based and fixed rule-based systems: Communication delay, exposing sensitive behavioral data, limited support for multi-user conflicts and decision transparency. In this study, the authors present an on-device preference graph reasoner that they deploy on an edge-based smart home gateway. The framework models the users, devices, contexts, preferences, actions, and application constraints as a heterogeneous graph and reasons on this graph to produce the personalized automation actions ranking. A conflict-resolution mechanism deals with conflicting preferences among household members, and a verification module will assess safety, privacy, energy and device limitations prior to execution. Evaluation is done based on decision accuracy, user acceptance rate, unsafe-action rejection rate, verification success rate, energy consumption, model size, memory use, inference latency, precision, recall, and F1-score. The proposed framework should enable responsive, explainable, privacy preserving, and verifiable automation that is feasible in smart home environments without a permanent cloud dependency nor cloud services.

title: Optimalisasi TinyBERT-Vosk Untuk Kontrol Suara Real-Time Robot Mecanum Raspberry Pi
authors: Gogor Christmass Setyawan; Surjawirawan Dwiputranto; Kristian Juri Damai Lase
venue: Jutisi Jurnal Ilmiah Teknik Informatika dan Sistem Informasi
abstract: This study targets low-latency on-device voice control on Raspberry Pi for a Mecanum 4WD robot.Key challenges include latency jitter, ASR accuracy under mild-moderate noise, and NLU compute load.We propose a fully local pipeline: Audio → WebRTC VAD → grammarconstrained (WFST) Vosk ASR → TinyBERT NLU distilled, INT8-quantized, and lightly pruned; complemented by a confidence gate, temperature scaling, a 1-360 numeral parser, and runtime tuning (threading, non-blocking queues, CPU affinity).Experiments on RPi 5 reduce end-to-end latency, improve ASR RTF and WER/CER, and lower CPU/memory and NLU latency without material loss in intent/slot accuracy, demonstrating resource-efficient real-time voice control with privacy preserved at the edge.

title: Context-Aware Edge-Cloud Multi‑Agent PHM Framework for Multi‑Tool CNC Turning Machines Using a Single Vibration Sensor
authors: BK Ramesh; S Shweta; Rachana Sreedhar
abstract: CNC turning machines operate under highly variable and context-dependent conditions, where multiple cutting tools and machine subsystems share a common structural vibration path. This creates a practical monitoring challenge: a single sensor captures a superposed vibration response, while tool wear and machine degradation evolve differently across tools, operations, and cutting conditions. This paper presents a context-aware edge-cloud multi-agent Prognostics and Health Management (PHM) framework for multi-tool CNC turning machines using a single spindle-mounted vibration sensor. The framework assigns a logical PHM agent to each tool, while a context router uses controller-side process information, such as tool identity, spindle speed, feed rate, and depth of cut, to transform the shared vibration stream into tool-specific feature streams. Each agent performs in situ baseline calibration, health indicator (HI) estimation, monitoring mode selection, online degradation tracking, and, where applicable, Remaining Useful Life (RUL) estimation. To improve deployment robustness, the library includes adaptive threshold estimation, online threshold refinement, and explicit handling of anomaly-dominant and degradation-dominant operating regimes. The framework is implemented as an edge-cloud architecture in which the edge performs feature extraction, context-aware routing, HI computation, and alert generation, while the cloud ingests telemetry and curated feature streams for visualization, storage, and lifecycle management. The study includes an industrial CNC case study with three tool types and an auxiliary evaluation on the UC Berkeley milling dataset. Results show that the framework can isolate tool-specific degradation behavior using a shared sensor, provide early warnings for rapidly degrading tools, and support low-latency edge deployment.

title: Neuromorphic AI-Based e-Skin for Emotion-Sensitive Humanoid Robots
authors: Shubham Gupta; Suhaib Ahmed
venue: International Electronic Conference on Applied Sciences (ASEC)
abstract: Humanoid robots operating in proximity to humans require the ability to perceive and interpret emotional cues conveyed through touch to achieve safe, natural, and socially intelligent interaction. Conventional tactile sensing systems primarily focus on force or pressure detection and cannot infer affective intent, while frame-based deep learning models often suffer from high latency and energy consumption when deployed on embedded platforms. To address these limitations, this paper presents a neuromorphic AI-based multimodal electronic skin (e-skin) framework for emotion-sensitive touch perception in humanoid robots. The proposed system integrates pressure, temperature, and electrostatic sensing with a bio-inspired signal conditioning pipeline and a Spiking Neural Network (SNN) for event-driven, low-power processing. A custom multimodal tactile dataset was collected using the proposed e-skin prototype to model four emotional touch interactions: stress, neutral, comfort, and affection. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves a high emotion classification accuracy of up to 92%, with an average accuracy of 88.75% across all classes. The neuromorphic SNN significantly reduces inference latency to approximately 8 ms, compared to 38 ms for a conventional CNN-based model, while maintaining energy-efficient operation suitable for edge deployment. The results validate the effectiveness of combining multimodal tactile sensing with neuromorphic processing to enable real-time, emotion-aware human–robot interaction.

title: RED: A Systematic Real-Time Scheduling Approach for Robotic Environmental Dynamics
authors: Zexin Li; Tao Ren; Xiaoxi He; Cong Liu
abstract: Intelligent robots are designed to effectively navigate dynamic and unpredictable environments laden with moving mechanical elements and objects. Such environment-induced dynamics, including moving obstacles, can readily alter the computational demand (e.g., the creation of new tasks) and the structure of workloads (e.g., precedence constraints among tasks) during runtime, thereby adversely affecting overall system performance. This challenge is amplified when multi-task inference is expected on robots operating under stringent resource and real-time constraints. To address such a challenge, we introduce RED, a systematic real-time scheduling approach designed to support multi-task deep neural network workloads in resource-limited robotic systems. It is designed to adaptively manage the Robotic Environmental Dynamics (RED) while adhering to real-time constraints. At the core of RED lies a deadline-based scheduler that employs an intermediate deadline assignment policy, effectively managing to change workloads and asynchronous inference prompted by complex, unpredictable environments. This scheduling framework also facilitates the flexible deployment of MIMONet (multi-input multi-output neural networks), which are commonly utilized in multi-tasking robotic systems to circumvent memory bottlenecks. Building on this scheduling framework, RED recognizes and leverages a unique characteristic of MIMONet: its weight-shared architecture. To further accommodate and exploit this feature, RED devises a novel and effective workload refinement and reconstruction process. This process ensures the scheduling framework's compatibility with MIMONet and maximizes efficiency. We have implemented RED on several widely used embedded and mobile platforms, including the NVIDIA Jetson Nano, TX2, Xavier, and Orin platforms. We evaluated its performance using workloads that span a broad range of settings typical in navigation robots. The experimental results demonstrate that RED surpasses existing approaches (often by a significant margin) across critical metrics such as throughput, timing correctness, interference robustness, adaptability, and overhead.

title: Lightweight visual servo detection method for inspection robots based on improved YOLOv5
authors: Shuo Wang; Longqing Fan; Yalei Pan; Linlin Wang; Li Wu; Rui Liu
abstract: Abstract Aiming at the demand for intelligent inspection of bolts on the train undercarriage, this paper proposes a robotic arm visual servo control method integrating lightweight deep learning and position-based visual servo (PBVS), to achieve high-precision automatic alignment of bolts in the robotic arm base coordinate system. To balance the real-time performance and accuracy requirements of embedded terminals, this paper introduces the lightweight PP-LCNet backbone network, CBAM attention mechanism, and EIOU loss function on the basis of YOLOv5s to form an improved YOLOv5s-PP-LCNet model, which significantly reduces the computational complexity and improves the accuracy of feature extraction. A dataset with multiple illumination conditions, multiple poses, and multiple backgrounds was constructed, and real-time inference experiments were conducted on Jetson Nano. The results show that the average precision of the algorithm reaches 98.79%, and the single-frame inference time is reduced to 35.7 ms while maintaining high detection accuracy, meeting the requirements of practical inspection applications. This method provides an efficient and low-cost technical approach for the intelligent detection of train undercarriage components.

title: Multi-Agent Smart Water Distribution with Computer Vision-Based Container Detection and AI-Driven Behavior Forecasting for Disaster Relief in Smart Cities
authors: Wuttachai Chumyen
abstract: This paper presents a self-developed multi-agent IoT water distribution system for disaster relief in smart cities, in which each smart dispenser operates as a fully agentic autonomous unit. The proposed design integrates an in-housetrained lightweight computer vision model (MobileNet-SSD) for real-time container presence and size estimation with a custom LSTM-based behavior forecasting engine to predict short-term demand patterns under dynamic emergency conditions. All agents coordinate via decentralized multi-agent reinforcement learning framework (Proximal Policy Optimization) over a LoRaWAN network, optimizing fairness, minimizing wait times, and maintaining resilience under packet-loss and bandwidth-constrained environments. The complete hardwaresoftware stack, from dataset acquisition and feature generation to model training and deployment, was developed entirely by the authors to enable on-device perception, prediction, and decision-making without reliance on cloud services. In laboratory trials with 20 agents serving 100 simulated requests, the system achieved a 94.5% dispensing success rate, 1.3 s average end-to-end latency, and a 32% improvement in fairness index over a heuristic baseline. A subsequent campus field deployment with 10 agents and 50 participants yielded 92% success, 1.5 s latency, and high user satisfaction (4.7/5). These results demonstrate that a purpose-built, agentic AI framework can deliver scalable, equitable, and resilient water access solutions for smart cities during disaster relief operations.

title: Edge AI-Based Intraoperative Image Segmentation for Robotic-Assisted Orthopedic Surgeries
authors: Sandip Desai; Swati Gopal Gawhale; Mohammad Sohail Pervez; Roopa B. Kakkeri; Prachi Janrao; Laxmikant Umate
abstract: Robotic-assisted orthopedic surgeries have revolutionized precision in joint replacement and fracture fixation. Intraoperative image segmentation remains a significant challenge due to high computational demands and the need for real-time processing. Traditional cloud-based solutions introduce latency, security concerns, and dependency on high-bandwidth internet, making them unsuitable for time-sensitive surgical procedures. Edge Artificial Intelligence (Edge AI) offers a transformative approach by enabling on-device computation, reducing latency, and improving the efficiency of intraoperative segmentation. This paper explores the integration of Edge AI for real-time intraoperative image segmentation in robotic-assisted orthopedic surgeries. We discuss the advantages of Edge AI in reducing reliance on external servers and ensuring high-speed, accurate segmentation directly at the surgical site. The study evaluates different deep learning architectures, including U-Net, DeepLabV3, and transformer-based models, optimized for edge deployment using techniques such as quantization, pruning, and knowledge distillation. A real-time processing pipeline is proposed, integrating Edge AI hardware such as NVIDIA Jetson Xavier and Google Coral TPU to process surgical images efficiently. Experimental results demonstrate that Edge AI-based segmentation achieves real-time inference with sub-100ms latency while maintaining high accuracy. The study highlights challenges such as hardware constraints, regulatory compliance, and model generalization across different patient anatomies. We discuss future research directions, including federated learning, augmented reality integration, and improved hardware acceleration. Overall, Edge AI has the potential to enhance robotic-assisted orthopedic surgeries by providing fast, accurate, and locally processed image segmentation, improving surgical precision and patient outcomes.

title: DEDUCE-Net: Efficient Semantic Segmentation on Embedded Systems for Autonomous Driving
authors: Nadeem Atif; Saquib Mazhar; Shaik Rafi Ahamed; Manas Kamal Bhuyan; M. T. Khan
venue: IEEE transactions on circuits and systems for artificial intelligence.
abstract: Semantic segmentation for autonomous driving is a time-critical application and thus requires an efficient solution. Consequently, designing segmentation models with low computational complexity and low power consumption is crucial for their practical deployment in resource-constrained edge devices. To achieve this, we present an ultra-lightweight network that strikes a decent balance between accuracy and efficiency. Specifically, we introduce the Details-Embedded Depthwise Unified Context Encoding (DEDUCE) module to jointly extract finer details and multi-scale short-range context from nearby regions to improve local understanding. To enable a holistic understanding, we propose a cascaded structure of dilated convolution and pooling-based pyramids. The resulting Pyramid over Pyramid (PoP) module introduces a new pyramid arrangement to maximize the effectiveness of individual pyramids due to their strategic positioning. Based on the DEDUCE and PoP modules, we propose DEDUCE-Net, which achieves extreme parameter efficiency while simultaneously achieving impressive accuracy. With only 0.16 million parameters, it achieves 70.32% mIoU on the cityscapes test set. Moreover, with resolution 512×1024, it achieves 238.5 and 25.76 FPS on RTX 3090 and Jetson Orin Nano (an embedded GPU), respectively. Furthermore, to achieve a power-efficient solution, we deployed the DEDUCE-Net on a ZCU102 board (Zynq UltraScale+MPSoC), where the power consumption is significantly lower compared to that on the Jetson Orin Nano (embedded GPU). Specifically, the power consumption on ZCU102 is 980 mW, whereas on Jetson Orin Nano, it is 3.7 W; more than 4× higher. The source code and trained models will be released to facilitate further research and applications.

title: Kinematic MeanFlow: One-Step Action Generation Policy for Robotic Foundation Models
authors: Jiawei Fan; Sifeng Wang; Yuqing Hou; Anbang Yao
abstract: In this paper, we study how to achieve one-step action generation in Robotic Foundation Models (RFMs), aiming to overcome the high inference latency of multi-step flow matching. MeanFlow provides a promising framework for this goal, yet its direct application leads to performance collapse. We discover that this stems from two distinctive dynamics exhibited in the RFM velocity field: (1) the ``local acceleration" exhibits stability early on, but surges sharply towards the end of the denoising process, and (2) the spread of its magnitudes across samples widens as denoising progresses. To address these issues, we introduce Kinematic MeanFlow (K-MF), a novel one-step action policy tailored for RFMs. Specifically, grounded in a kinematic identity, K-MF decouples the time derivative term in the MeanFlow formulation into two sub-interval terms separated by an intermediate point. This decoupled formulation enables the two terms to capture early-stage and late-stage denoising dynamics, respectively, while mitigating the error amplification across the process. As a result, our K-MF empowers RFMs to achieve one-step action generation in both training from scratch and fine-tuning paradigms across diverse tasks, while outperforming multi-step flow matching in most settings. In terms of inference efficiency, K-MF reduces action-head latency of GR00T-N1.6 by 67.5%~74.4% across L40 and Jetson Orin in eager and compiled modes, yielding end-to-end latency reductions of 30.3%~54.9%. Code will be available at https://github.com/IntelChina-AI/K-MF.

title: GPU-Based Parallel Computation of Multi-Set Dynamics for Articulated Robots
authors: Jechan Jeon; 장유선; Yonghwan Oh
venue: IEEE/ASME International Conference on Advanced Intelligent Mechatronics
abstract: Predictive controllers that incorporate full-body dynamics have long been constrained by a fundamental trade-off between model fidelity and computational feasibility. We present GPU-ARBML, a GPU library that evaluates articulated full-body dynamics in large batches. The library adopts an asynchronous pipeline integrating pinned memory and CUDA streams to decouple CPU-GPU communication. This architecture effectively minimizes control-loop jitter while ensuring high determinism. Benchmarks on a complex 29-DOF floating-base model show that GPU-ARBML outperforms state-of-the-art CPU libraries in multi-set computations, exhibiting sub-linear growth in iteration time as the number of rollouts increases. Integrated with an MPPI controller, GPU-ARBML is validated on 6-DOF and 7-DOF arms in both simulation and hardware, sustaining 500 Hz real-time control on embedded hardware (NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin). Furthermore, the library’s versatility is demonstrated through a simulation study of a two-wheeled legged robot’s balancing control. These results support the practical deployment of floating-base models.

title: Real-Time Gesture Recognition for Medical Human-Robot Interaction
authors: Sonja Stabenow; Lukas Bernhard; Klaus J. Bengler; Dirk Wilhelm
abstract: This work addresses key limitations in state-of-the-art hand-landmark detection to enable reliable, gesture-based human-robot interaction in healthcare settings. Current gesture recognition applications fail to account for the unique characteristics of clinical scenarios, such as the requirement for healthcare professionals to wear medical gloves throughout critical stages of patient care. To mitigate this domain gap, we introduce the novel medical-glove dataset MedGlove1k and demonstrate its effectiveness in adapting hand-landmark detection models to the medical domain, while meeting crucial requirements for low latency and edge-computing deployment. After fine-tuning on MedGlove1k, our YOLO-based detection model achieves a pose$\text{m A P}_{50}$of$\text{9 7. 4} {\%}$while maintaining an inference speed of$\approx \text{2 0 0}$frames per second, indicating an improvement of 42.4% in pose estimation performance over non-domain-adapted baselines. We further validate our approach under edge-deployment conditions, observing full-architecture latencies of$\text{3 3 0. 0 2 ~ m s}$on an NVIDIA Jetson Nano. We demonstrate the system's practical viability by successfully integrating it into a robotic platform for real-time human-robot interaction, achieving a 96.8% success rate for end-to-end gesture-based robot control. As a foundation for future applications in healthcare settings, we make our MedGlove1k dataset publicly available and provide our detection architecture as a ROS2-based landmark and gesture recognition framework.

title: Cross-domain bearing fault diagnosis for electric multi-rotor UAVs based on soft prompt-guided graph neural network and domain-adaptive feature alignment
authors: Zhaoqiang Lv; Chengyu Hou; Di Chen
abstract: Abstract The rotor motor bearings of electric multi-rotor UAVs are subject to combined excitation from aerodynamic disturbances and airframe-coupled vibrations. When diagnostic models trained under laboratory conditions are deployed in real flight scenarios, distribution shift destabilizes classification boundaries. This cross-domain generalization problem is the core obstacle limiting intelligent bearing diagnosis in practice. To address this, we propose a cross-domain bearing fault diagnosis framework based on a soft prompt-guided graph neural network and domain-adaptive feature alignment. The framework maps time-domain, frequency-domain, and time–frequency features of vibration signals to graph nodes. A domain-aware graph structure modeling method based on soft prompt embedding is developed: domain-aware soft prompt vectors are embedded during node initialization, enabling the adaptive adjacency matrix to be dynamically constructed under dual constraints from signal feature correlations and domain membership. A dynamic prompt generation network, driven by batch statistics, together with an exponential moving average mechanism for stabilizing target-domain statistics under non-stationary conditions and small batch sizes, eliminates dependence on explicit domain labels. A cross-domain diagnostic optimization method based on attention-weighted maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) is also proposed: an attention weight network generates dimension-wise weight vectors to construct a weighted MMD loss, coordinated with a progressive scheduling strategy to balance classification and alignment objectives. Experiments across cross-speed, cross-load, and cross-dataset transfer tasks on five public benchmark datasets and one local multi-rotor UAV dataset, supplemented by a multi-physics simulation study, demonstrate that the proposed framework attains competitive Macro- F 1 scores among the comparison methods, consistently achieving the highest Macro- F 1 across the five public benchmark datasets. Ablation studies validate the necessity of each core component, and noise robustness analysis confirms that the framework maintains leading performance with small variance under low signal-to-noise ratios, demonstrating its effectiveness and robustness. Deployment efficiency analysis on Intel Core i7 and NVIDIA Jetson Xavier NX platforms confirms millisecond-level inference latency that meets typical UAV onboard requirements.

title: VLM-based high-level action planner for mobile robots
authors: Víctor Marín Jiménez
venue: UPCommons institutional repository (Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya)
abstract: This thesis explores the use of a visual-language model (VLM) based approach for the highlevel action planning of a mobile robot, instantiated in the case of an autonomous vehicle. The approach is integrated in a hierarchical framework that decouples the perception, high-level planning and low-level control into connected modules. These modules communicate with each other using ROS2. The framework operates as follows: the perception module fuses the vehicle’s sensor data, and generates a structured scene context that grounds the VLM model in its surroundings. The decision-making module combines this sensorial data with an image, from the vehicle’s frontal camera, into a prompt. Then, it queries the VLM and obtains a discrete driving action. The behavior of the model is specified through natural language and sent to the VLM as the system’s prompt. Finally, the low-level control module translates the high-level action into a specific vehicle behavior through CARLA’s Traffic Manager, and wraps it in a dedicated layer of safeguards that prevents dangerous maneuvers arising from models hallucinations or inference latency. The central hypotheses of this thesis are, first, that the proposed architecture is capable of guiding the vehicle taking well-grounded mid-term decisions, while the low-level control layer acts as a safety substrate that keeps navigation viable through the model’s long latency periods; and second, that the framework is model agnostic, with the quality of the decisions taken scaling with the capability of the model. Furthermore, the thesis investigates whether the visual input improves the navigation planning by providing real-world grounding, enhancing the model’s reasoning. The framework is validated in CARLA simulator, considering a single navigation environment, Town10HD, which reproduces an inner-city urban setting that challenges the agent’s reasoning capabilities. Two VLM models are proposed for the study: Qwen3.5:2B, as an on-device baseline model, and Claude Haiku 4.5 as an upper-bound cloud reference. Five scenarios of increasing complexity are considered: a free run, a run with ambient traffic present, a road obstruction, a pedestrian suddenly crossing, and the approach of an ambulance. The decisions of the VLMbased approach are subsequently evaluated both qualitatively, through visual inspection, and quantitatively through key metrics such as valid-call rate, fallback rate and hallucination instances. The results obtained showed how both models are capable of successfully guiding the vehicle. Despite the instability shown by the baseline, the control layer and its safeguards kept the resulting driving viable and close to that of the reference, supporting the role of the architecture as a model-agnostic safety substrate. The difference in output quality between the two models (91.5% valid calls for the baseline versus 100.0% for the reference) is absorbed before it reaches the vehicle. The tests are consistent with our underlying hypothesis, decision quality scales with model capability. Yet the outcome divergence remains mild because the control layer compensates for the baseline model, showing that the framework itself bridges the gap between both models. This compensation, however, has a clear boundary, as the safety layer rejects malformed or unstable outputs, but it cannot correct a decision that is well-formed and wrong. This fact was clearly observed in the pedestrian scenario, when the baseline model moved recklessly towards a pedestrian still in the front cone while emitting a valid action that no safeguard could flag. Finally, contribution of visual support could not be isolated under the current design and a dedicated ablation study is required to draw a firm conclusion on this matter.

title: DEVELOPMENT OF AN OPTIMIZED YOLO-BASED REAL-TIME VISION SYSTEM FOR OBJECT DETECTION IN INDUSTRIAL CLEANING ROBOTS
authors: IFEKA OLUKEMI IBIYEMI; BUSAYO TEMITOPE ACHORI; GABRIEL FUNMINIYI OLULEYE; IDOWU OLAYINKA BISI
venue: International Journal of Science Research and Technology
abstract: Industrial cleaning robots operating in dynamic and cluttered environments require robust, accurate, and low-latency object detection systems to ensure safe navigation, efficient task execution, and collision avoidance. Traditional vision-based detection methods often fail to meet real-time performance constraints when deployed on embedded robotic platforms with limited computational resources. This research presents the development of an optimized YOLO-based real-time vision system for object detection in industrial cleaning robots. The proposed system leverages advanced variants of the YOLO (You Only Look Once) deep learning architecture, selected for its single-stage detection capability and high inference speed. Model optimization techniques including network pruning, quantization, input resolution tuning, anchor box recalibration, and hardware-aware training were implemented to balance detection accuracy and computational efficiency. Transfer learning was employed using pre-trained weights, followed by fine-tuning on a domain-specific dataset consisting of industrial floor environments with obstacles such as debris, cables, tools, liquid spills, and human presence. To ensure real-time deployment, the system was integrated with embedded GPU hardware and optimized using parallel processing and model acceleration frameworks. Performance evaluation was conducted using standard metrics including mean Average Precision (mAP), precision-recall curves, F1-score, and inference latency (frames per second). Experimental results demonstrate that the optimized YOLO model achieves high detection accuracy while maintaining real-time performance under industrial lighting variations, occlusions, and dynamic object movement. The developed vision system significantly enhances robotic perception capabilities, enabling improved obstacle avoidance, adaptive cleaning path planning, and operational safety. The study contributes a scalable and deployable framework for integrating lightweight deep learning-based object detection into autonomous industrial service robots. Future work may explore multimodal sensor fusion, edge-AI deployment optimization, and continual learning for long-term industrial adaptability.

title: Deep Learning for Real-Time Fault Detection in Wireless Robotic Systems
authors: Chijioke Cyriacus Ekechi
venue: International Journal of Future Engineering Innovations
abstract: Wireless robotic systems are increasingly deployed in complex and dynamic environments where uninterrupted operation is critical. Ensuring real-time fault detection is essential to maintain the safety, reliability, and autonomy of these systems. Traditional rule-based and statistical fault detection methods often fall short in capturing the intricate, non-linear behaviors inherent in modern robotic operations, particularly under wireless and resource-constrained conditions. This study investigates the application of deep learning for real-time fault detection in wireless robotic systems, aiming to develop a robust framework capable of identifying faults across sensors, actuators, and communication channels. The research integrates simulation tools such as ROS, Gazebo, and NS-3 to generate realistic robotic telemetry under controlled fault scenarios. Public datasets including the NASA C-MAPSS and bearing datasets are utilized alongside sensor logs from simulated robotic environments. Deep learning models—specifically Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Long Short-Term Memory networks (LSTMs), and Autoencoders—are implemented and evaluated for fault classification and anomaly detection. Experimental results demonstrate that these models achieve high detection accuracy and low inference latency, outperforming traditional methods and proving suitable for real-time edge deployment. The findings underscore the potential of deep learning to enhance the resilience and intelligence of future autonomous robotic platforms, laying the groundwork for self-monitoring, adaptive, and fault-tolerant robotic systems.
